questions.stemHtml: A child with absent thymus and presented with a tetany. Which of the following marked areas in the given image is defective in this Condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
C
  • The given clinical features suggest the diagnosis of DiGeorge syndrome. Thymus and parathyroid are absent in this patient suggesting defect in 3rd pharyngeal pouch marked as ‘C' in the given image.


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 296,297.

questions.stemHtml: Covid may spread to meninges and lead to intracranial complications through which of the following marked areas?
questions.solutionHtml:
C
  • SARS-COV2 reaches Brian via cribriform plate and olfactory bulb marked in the given figure as ‘C'
  • Neurological sequelae to severe Covid-19 include encephalitis, demyelination, neuropathy and stroke.
  • Refractory respiratory failure can occur if the virus invades medullary cardio respiratory center.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-566,567.

questions.stemHtml: Structure forming the superior boundary of foramen marked is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Caudate lobe of liver
  • The structure marked in the given image is epiploic foramen. Caudate lobe of the liver forms the superior border of epiploic foramen.
  • Epiploic foramen connects lesser sac to the greater sac.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-336,338.

questions.stemHtml: A woman presented to the hospital with loss of sensation in right upper and lower limbs. She also complains of shooting pain from her fingers, the right shoulder and a burning sensation when she touches cold water. Motor functions are normal. Which of the following structures is likely to be involved?
questions.solutionHtml:
B

The given clinical features suggest involvement of thalamus.

Thalamus pain syndrome/Dejerine Roussy syndrome

  • Due to occlusion of thalamus and thalamo geniculate branches
  • It is characterised by C/L hemisensory loss which starts as numbness and progresses to cause severe burning pain in the affected regions.
  • The pain responds poorly to analgesics
  • Anticonvulsants such as Carbamazepine or gabapentin or tricyclic antidepressants may be beneficial.


https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32119377/

questions.stem: Which of the following are the branches of anterior division of the internal Iliac artery?Superior gluteal arteryInferior gluteal arterySuperior vesical arteryMiddle rectal arteryInferior vesical arteryVaginal arterySelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2, 3, 4, 5 and 6

Internal Iliac artery divides into anterior and posterior trunks at the superior border of greater sciatic foramen.

Branches of anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery

  1. Obturator artery
  2. Superior vesical artery
  3. Inferior vesical artery
  4. Inferior gluteal artery
  5. Middle rectal artery
  6. Vaginal artery (females)
  7. Uterine artery (females)
  8. Internal pudendal artery


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e80, 1464.e81.

questions.stemHtml: A 6 month old boy was brought to the casualty with seizures. The pediatrician does CSF sampling through the marked structure. What are the structures punctured by the pediatrician?
questions.solutionHtml:
Scalp, dura, arachnoid
  • The marked structure in the image is anterior fontanelle.
  • The structures pierced in ventricular tapping are scalp, dura and arachnoid.
  • A 25 gauge butterfly needle is inserted through the anterolateral aspect of the anterior fontanelle (away from the midline, avoiding the superior sagittal sinus)


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e80, 1464.e81.
